title: Egg omelet with cheese and meat

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet prepared with cooking spray, enriched with cheese and meat. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while cheese and meat add rich flavor and additional nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cooking spray allows you to cook with minimal oil, reducing the dish’s calorie count.
Cheese adds calcium and vitamin D, which support bone health.
Meat (such as ham or bacon) supplies iron and vitamin B12, essential for blood formation.
The omelet can be ready in 5‑7 minutes, making it a quick breakfast or snack.
Variations of omelets exist worldwide: French omelet, Spanish tortilla, and Japanese tamagoyaki.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs contain all essential amino acids, making the omelet a complete protein source.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Eggs and meat provide vitamins B2, B6, and B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium and vitamin D, supporting strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Meat supplies heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Low saturated fat when using spray
items.content: Cooking spray lets you limit added fat, lowering the overall saturated fat content of the dish.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor their intake.

items.title: Sodium in cheese and meat
items.content: Processed meats and many cheeses are high in salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Quality of cooking spray
items.content: Some sprays contain propellants or additives; choose products free from harmful chemicals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, garnished with fresh herbs, tomatoes, or avocado. It works well as a standalone dish or as a filling for sandwiches, wraps, or tacos.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a microwave or skillet with a light spray to prevent drying out.
